name: The Listening Pit and the Gates

pages.title: Placement is the ritual
pages.text: Devices that claim to be rites have to be arranged, not scattered. Seven shapes, all rotation-independent: the Stone Font, the Listening Pit, the Rite Circle, the Voice Ring, the Shatter Array and both gates. A Voice Ring of totems at radius 3 around a Pulse Resonator is opt-in — a scattered heap still works, but counts at most five voices.

pages.title: Stone Font
pages.text: The starter rite. A font and four chalk marks asks for cobblestone at 4 Pulse a second. Brace it and bring Earth for stone. Add Fire and Water for obsidian at 24 Pulse a second, or feed 250 mB water and 250 mB lava for the same obsidian at 6.

pages.title: Listening Pit
pages.text: Stone, four Anchor Stones, chalk to the middle, a Resonance Mesh, an Ancestral Cache and Earth in reach. Metals come out raw or as grit; gems skip the fire. A sample on top is a filter, never an ingredient. Mining stays cheaper; the pit buys walking away from it.

pages.title: One voice, one source
pages.text: Earth is the Drumheart. Fire is the Ember Horn (furnace fuel, up to 20/s). Air is the Wind Harp (altitude, sky, weather). Water is the Wave Drum (adjacent or piped). Spirit is the Wake Bell (nearby deaths). Loom is the Loom Anchor (1/s per distinct voice). Pulse Cairns hold 4,000 each, five to a column.

pages.title: Way Gate and Far Gate
pages.text: The Gate Drum stays the portable way into the March. A Way Gate is a five-by-five frame, 20 Pulse a traveller, linked within 64 blocks. A Far Gate is taller, braced, Loom-voiced, linked with a Gate Sigil, 120 Pulse a traveller. Players, mobs and items all pass. `/tribalpower gate list`.
